method: manual web verification against rank 2-3 authorities; no bank records modified

records.keyClaim: Uterine artery (internal iliac) is the primary uterine blood supply.

citations.quote: The uterine artery is a branch of the internal iliac artery... main blood vessels that supply blood to the uterus.
The uterus receives its primary blood supply from the uterine and ovarian arteries, both originating from the anterior branch of the internal iliac artery.

records.keyClaim: Pancreas occupies left hypochondrium and epigastrium.

citations.quote: traverses the epigastric, left hypochondriac, and a small portion of the umbilical regions
Epigastrium: stomach, liver, pancreas, duodenum

records.keyClaim: Uterine sensory signals travel via hypogastric nerves to T10-L1.

citations.quote: Sensory signals from the uterus travel through the hypogastric nerves to spinal levels T10 to L1.

records.reviewerNote: Sympathetic efferents cited as T11-T12; afferent claim T10-L1 directly supported.

records.keyClaim: Pancreatic tail is the intraperitoneal part.

citations.quote: It is the only intraperitoneal part of the pancreas, contained within the splenorenal ligament.
the pancreatic tail is intraperitoneal

records.keyClaim: Aorta lies posterior to 3rd and 4th duodenal parts.

citations.quote: Between the origins of superior mesenteric and inferior mesenteric arteries - left renal vein, the uncinate process of the pancreas and 3 part of the duodenum
The fourth (ascending) part (2.5 cm), begins to the left of the abdominal aorta

records.reviewerNote: 3rd part anterior to aorta confirmed; 4th part is lateral (left of aorta), not strictly posterior. Source page must confirm the bank's exact E wording before approval.

records.keyClaim: Ureters end at the level of the pubic tubercle.

citations.quote: The ureters lack reliable anatomical landmarks to mark their location besides the 3 physiologic constrictions.
turns anteromedially opposite the ischial spine ... to reach the fundus of the bladder

records.reviewerNote: No rank 2-3 source supports the pubic tubercle as the ureteric termination level; ischial spine is the cited turn landmark. Possible key mismatch - source-page check required, do not approve.

records.keyClaim: Rectus sheath formed by all three lateral aponeuroses.

citations.quote: The fascial coverings of the external oblique, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis muscles comprise the rectus sheath.

records.keyClaim: Renal arteries arise just posterior to the pancreas.

citations.quote: The left renal artery courses ... posterior to ... the body of the pancreas; right renal artery courses posterior to ... head of the pancreas and second part of the duodenum.
arise from the lateral aspect of the abdominal aorta, typically at L1/L2, immediately inferior to the SMA

records.keyClaim: Omental bursa lies posterior to stomach and liver.

citations.quote: lesser sac ... between the stomach and the pancreas ... superior omental recess extends between the medial aspect of the caudate lobe of the liver and the diaphragm.
The lesser sac lies posterior to the stomach and lesser omentum.

records.keyClaim: Infraduodenal CBD runs in a groove posterior to pancreatic head.

citations.quote: the bile duct lies in a groove on the posterosuperior surface of the head
The common bile duct passes dorsal to the first part of the duodenum lying in a groove either within or posterior to the head of the pancreas

records.keyClaim: Spleen is NOT a posterior relation of transverse colon.

citations.quote: Posterior to the transverse colon are the descending part of the duodenum, the head of the pancreas, the mesentery, the duodenojejunal flexure, and the small intestine.
visceral surface related to the stomach, left colic flexure, and left kidney

records.rank3Note: transverse-colon posterior list from rank-4 overview; spleen relations from rank-3 Dartmouth chapter
records.reviewerNote: Spleen relates to splenic flexure laterally, not posterior to transverse colon.

records.keyClaim: Aorta terminates as right and left common iliacs.

citations.quote: The abdominal aorta bifurcates into the right and left common iliac arteries close to the L4 vertebral level.

records.keyClaim: SMA occlusion threatens jejunum and ileum.

citations.quote: provides blood flow to the third portion of the duodenum, the jejunum, the ileum, the cecum, the ascending colon... splenic flexure is a watershed area

records.reviewerNote: Splenic flexure is watershed (less likely than jejunum/ileum); stomach/foregut supplied by coeliac.

records.keyClaim: Spleen lies at ribs 9-11 posteriorly.

citations.quote: typically spanning the ninth to 11th ribs.
ribs 9 to 11 on the left-hand side

records.keyClaim: Ductus deferens is the continuation of the epididymis.

citations.quote: a fibromuscular tube that is a continuation of the epididymis
The ductus deferens is the continuation of the tail of the epididymis.
they give rise to the epididymis, vas deferens, and seminal vesicles

records.reviewerNote: Embryology nuance: both derive from the Wolffian duct (NBK557818); the question tests anatomical continuation, which key D answers.

records.keyClaim: L1 root supplies transversus abdominis and internal oblique.

citations.quote: iliohypogastric/ilioinguinal (L1) ... motor branches to the inferior portions of the transversus abdominis, external oblique, and internal oblique muscles.

records.reviewerNote: Gluteus medius/minimus are superior gluteal (L4-S1), excluded.

records.keyClaim: Scrotal skin supplied by L1 (anterior) and S2-S3 (posterior/inferior).

citations.quote: Anterior scrotal nerves (ilioinguinal L1) supply the anterior surface; posterior scrotal nerves (pudendal S2-4); perineal branches of posterior cutaneous nerve of thigh (S2,3).

citations.authority: UAMS Nerves of Pelvis and Perineum
citations.quote: anterior scrotal n. ... skin of the anterior aspect of the scrotum ... continuation of the ilioinguinal n.; genitofemoral n. (L1-L2) ... skin of the anterior scrotum

records.keyClaim: Kidneys extend T12-L3.

citations.quote: paired retroperitoneal organs located between the T12 and L3 vertebrae.

records.keyClaim: Pancreatic body at L1 (transpyloric plane).

citations.quote: located at the level of the transpyloric plane (L1)
crossing the bodies of the L1 and L2 vertebrae

records.reviewerNote: Body spans L1-L2; L1 is the best option (neck at transpyloric plane).

records.keyClaim: Uterine tubes open into the peritoneal cavity; ectopics commonest in ampulla, not isthmus.

citations.quote: most frequently located at the ampulla region (70%)
ampulla 70%, isthmic 12%, fimbrial 11%

records.reviewerNote: Eliminates B (tube ~10cm), C (opening = infundibulum/fimbria), D (isthmus is narrowest), E (isthmus second, not first).

records.keyClaim: Perinephric abscess lies between renal capsule and Gerota fascia.

citations.quote: affects the renal capsule and Gerota's fascia
located between the capsule of the kidney and the Gerota fascia

records.keyClaim: Morison pouch = right subhepatic (hepatorenal) space.

citations.quote: Right supramesocolic space is further divided into right subphrenic space, right subhepatic space (hepatorenal pouch or Morrison's pouch), and lesser sac.

records.keyClaim: Renal artery derives from abdominal aorta.

citations.quote: arise from the lateral aspect of the abdominal aorta, typically at L1/L2

records.keyClaim: Pancreatic neck tumour metastasises first to liver via portal drainage.

citations.quote: portal vein is formed behind the neck of the pancreas by the union of the splenic and superior mesenteric veins
portal vein and SMV involvement is common in pancreatic head/neck cancer due to anatomical proximity

records.reviewerNote: Portal blood flows to liver first.

records.keyClaim: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve supplies lateral thigh skin.

citations.quote: supplying cutaneous sensation to the anterolateral and lateral thigh

records.keyClaim: Iliohypogastric supplies posterolateral gluteal skin.

citations.quote: gives off a lateral cutaneous branch ... to supply the skin ... that overlies the buttocks and ilium

records.keyClaim: Retrocaecal is the most common appendix position.

citations.quote: The retrocecal position is by far the most common.
retrocecal position ... most common anatomical variant

records.reviewerNote: Some populations show pelvic predominance; retrocaecal is the exam-standard answer.

records.keyClaim: Uncinate tumour most likely compresses SMA.

citations.quote: Posterior to the artery lies the uncinate process of the pancreas
The uncinate process ... projects medially and wraps around the superior mesenteric vessels

records.reviewerNote: SMV/portal vein also adjacent; among options SMA is the vessel the uncinate wraps.

records.keyClaim: Glans penis drains primarily to deep inguinal nodes.

citations.quote: deep nodes receive drainage from the glans penis or clitoris
deep lymphatics ... along with the glans penis

records.keyClaim: Jejunal/ileal (midgut) pain refers to the umbilical region.

citations.quote: Pain arising ... from the midgut in the umbilical area; The small intestine ... produces midline, periumbilical visceral pain (T10)

records.keyClaim: Pancreatic neck tumour most likely compresses portal vein.

citations.quote: The neck of the pancreas ... lies in front of the SMV, splenic vein, and portal vein junction.
Portal vein formed posterior to the neck of the pancreas
The portal vein is formed behind the neck of the pancreas by the union of the splenic vein and the superior mesenteric vein

records.keyClaim: Aortic bifurcation ~2.5cm below the umbilicus (L4).

citations.quote: typically located at the lower border of the L4 vertebral body, approximately 2.5 cm below the umbilicus.
bifurcation at the L4 vertebral level

records.reviewerNote: Hurd 1992 notes umbilicus is often at/above the bifurcation; 2.5cm-below remains the exam convention.

records.keyClaim: Iliacus innervated by femoral nerve.

citations.quote: The iliacus is innervated by the femoral nerve
The femoral nerve innervates the sartorius, pectineus, quadriceps femoris, and iliacus muscle

records.keyClaim: IVC formed at L5 by common iliac confluence.

citations.quote: formed by the confluence of the right and left common iliac veins ... at the L5 vertebral level.

records.keyClaim: Inferior epigastric artery does NOT pass through the inguinal canal.

citations.authority: StatPearls Inguinal Canal region (NBK470204, via existing batch-11 evidence)
citations.quote: ilioinguinal and genitofemoral nerves pass within it; the deep ring is lateral to the epigastric vessels

records.reviewerNote: Artery runs in rectus sheath, medial to deep ring; cord/round ligament + genital branch + ilioinguinal nerve do traverse.

records.keyClaim: Spleen occupies left hypochondrium.

citations.quote: located in the left hypochondriac region between the diaphragm and gastric fundus

records.keyClaim: Ejaculatory duct = ductus deferens + seminal vesicle duct.

citations.quote: formed by the union of the duct from the seminal vesicle and the ductus (vas) deferens
seminal vesicle ultimately converging with an ampullae to form the ejaculatory duct

records.keyClaim: Female urethra opens in the vestibule between the labia minora.

citations.quote: the urethra opens within the vulvar vestibule ... The area between the labia minora is known as the vulvar vestibule.
4 cm long tubular structure that begins at the bladder neck and terminates at the vaginal vestibule

records.reviewerNote: Eliminates A (male longer), B (begins at bladder neck, not apex), D/E (sphincter/vaginal relations misstated).

records.keyClaim: Duodenal supply primarily gastroduodenal + superior mesenteric arcades.

citations.quote: GDA ... gives off ... anterior/posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery ... Anterior and posterior branches of the SPDA and IPDA join ... supplying ... the first, second, and third parts of the duodenum
The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery arises from the SMA and, along with the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery, supplies the head of the pancreas

records.rank3Note: SMA half from rank-3 NBK519560; gastroduodenal half from rank-4 Medscape overview
records.reviewerNote: Rank-3 coverage is partial (SMA/inferior half); the gastroduodenal half rests on rank-4 overview. Source-page check decides approval.

records.keyClaim: CBD + pancreatic duct unite as ampulla of Vater.

citations.quote: joins the bile duct to form the hepatopancreatic ampulla, which opens into the descending part of the duodenum.

records.keyClaim: Inferior epigastric vessels differentiate direct vs indirect hernia.

citations.quote: the deep ring is lateral to the epigastric vessels

records.reviewerNote: Indirect sac passes lateral (through deep ring), direct medial to the vessels.

records.keyClaim: IVC lies posterior to 1st and 3rd duodenal parts.

citations.quote: superior (1st): ... anterior to the bile duct, the gastroduodenal artery, the portal vein, and the IVC; horizontal (3rd): ... anterior to ... the IVC, the abdominal aorta

records.keyClaim: Liver lymph drains primarily to coeliac nodes.

citations.quote: The liver drains its lymph into the hepatic, caval, posterior mediastinal, and celiac lymph nodes.
drain into the hepatic nodes and subsequently into the coeliac group

records.keyClaim: Transversus abdominis muscle is NOT enclosed by rectus sheath (categorical exam answer).

citations.quote: contains both the rectus abdominis muscle and the pyramidalis muscle ... thoracoabdominal nerves ... epigastric vessels

records.reviewerNote: Caveat (existing batch-11 note): one study found transversus fibres within the sheath superiorly - exam-categorical answer stands, note retained.

records.keyClaim: Ilioinguinal supplies upper medial thigh skin.

citations.quote: provides sensory innervation to the upper anteromedial thigh region

records.keyClaim: Transverse mesocolon divides greater sac into supra/infracolic compartments.

citations.quote: further divided into two compartments by the ... transverse mesocolon: Supracolic ... Infracolic

records.reviewerNote: No rank<=3 citation; approval requires source-page plus rank<=3 agreement.

records.keyClaim: BPH arises in the transitional zone.

citations.quote: The transitional zone ... This is the zone where benign prostatic hypertrophy occurs
stromal and epithelial cell proliferation in the prostate transition zone

records.keyClaim: Ilioinguinal innervates internal oblique + transversus abdominis.

citations.quote: motor innervation of the transverse abdominis and internal oblique muscles

records.keyClaim: Temporal lobe lies inferior to the lateral sulcus.

citations.quote: It is found inferior to the lateral fissure, also known as the Sylvian fissure or the lateral sulcus.

records.keyClaim: Post-traumatic CSF rhinorrhoea implicates ethmoid (cribriform) fracture.

citations.quote: fractures of the cribriform plate can easily tear the dura and lead to leakage of CSF into the nasal cavity
fracture of the cribriform plate ... allows cerebrospinal fluid to extravasate into the nasal passages

records.reviewerNote: Cribriform plate is part of the ethmoid bone (NBK544328).
